title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.

title: Composite cathode comprising titanium disulfide and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. Polysulfide dissolution from the titanium disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The titanium disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the titanium disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, carbon nanotubes, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 200 mPa s to 10000 mPa s.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The capacity retention of 90% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. With 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, porous carbon, and polyacrylic acid is described. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A separator coated with porous carbon traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The active material sulfur is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The composite shows a capacity of 1200 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. A 10 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range. The anode support contains nickel oxide and yttria-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the yttria-stabilized zirconia cell.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 600 to 750 degrees C. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a molybdenum disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 100 cycles. A separator coated with porous carbon traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 0.8 W/cm2. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The anode support contains nickel oxide and gadolinium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 650 to 800 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria with a thickness of 3 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The thin 3 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. A lithium-sulfur battery with the iron sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The active material iron sulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The iron sulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The iron sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising iron sulfide, porous carbon, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the iron sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria with a thickness of 5 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C. The samarium-doped ceria solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. A power density of 0.8 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range. The thin 5 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 0.8 W/cm2. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising samarium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The anode support contains nickel oxide and samarium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. The lanthanum strontium manganite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 650 to 800 degrees C. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. A 5 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a surface mount capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode and a lead frame. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor rated at 10 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the niobium anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 150 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polypyrrole particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Potentiometric ammonia sensor having an auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a lanthanum strontium manganite electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the ammonia concentration. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The ceramic is gadolinium-doped ceria and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for ammonia.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The confinement of nickel sulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode delivering 600 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The capacity retention of 92% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor element with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer and a carbon cathode layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a tantalum solid electrolytic capacitor with a low equivalent series resistance and a high rated voltage. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. A capacitance of 47 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the tantalum capacitor. The anode body is a sintered pellet of tantalum powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles doped with p-toluenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The titanium disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into ketjen black at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The content of P2O5 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 5 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 600 to 750 degrees C. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 5 micrometers and a relative density of 98%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 600 to 750 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 5 micrometers. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for ammonia with improved response time
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which ammonia is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The protective layer improves the durability of the lanthanum fluoride sensor in an exhaust gas. The ceramic is lanthanum fluoride and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for ammonia. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of ammonia concentration at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed.
