title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LGPS material. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 5 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The solid electrolyte layer of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The reversible cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Amperometric sulfur dioxide sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of sodium nitrite that converts the sulfur dioxide concentration into an ionic activity. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of sulfur dioxide concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The multilayer structure with the lanthanum fluoride ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of sulfur dioxide.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Disclosed is a UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The reversible cell with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 3 micrometers. A 3 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 500 to 650 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 98% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 5 micrometers and a relative density of 98%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 650 to 800 degrees C. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. With 1 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 600 to 750 degrees C. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. The cell can be operated at 600 to 750 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. A 10 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 3 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The cell can be operated at 600 to 750 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 600 to 750 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing alumina nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polycarbonate based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polycarbonate and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyacrylonitrile and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyacrylonitrile matrix, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. The aluminum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The anode body is a sintered pellet of aluminum powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 20 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The capacitor withstands 105 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a aluminum anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 10 V.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The LLTO and LATP material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1230 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The capacitor rated at 16 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. The solid electrolyte is the conductive polymer layer that serves as the true cathode of the capacitor. The capacitor has a capacitance of 470 microfarads, a rated voltage of 16 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 5 milliohms at 100 kHz. The polypyrrole is doped with p-toluenesulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. The anode body is a sintered pellet of niobium powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polypyrrole particles doped with p-toluenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.3 to 0.75. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The thin 10 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 500 to 650 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The stack shows stable operation over 50 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C. The anode support contains nickel oxide and lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 10 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The confinement of lithium sulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising ketjen black; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 30 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In the trigonal structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

assignee_raw: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
assignee_db_group: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a magnesium additive. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved electrochemical window and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a niobium solid electrolytic capacitor with a low equivalent series resistance and a high rated voltage. The equivalent series resistance is 20 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 20 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body. The niobium capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a niobium anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 6.3 V.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.
