The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate solid electrolyte for detecting sulfur dioxide
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which sulfur dioxide is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for sulfur dioxide. The limiting current is proportional to the sulfur dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The sensing electrode comprises gold and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The gold electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting sulfur dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate; a sensing electrode comprising gold disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A precursor of the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 500 to 650 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.2 W/cm2. The solid electrolyte of scandia-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 98% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 1.2 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Multilayer ceramic gas sensor element and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of ammonia concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The auxiliary electrode of sodium carbonate makes the sensor selective to ammonia against interfering gases. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The ammonia sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

assignee_raw: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
assignee_db_group: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS HNRIEM
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LATP, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and beta-Li3PS4. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The warm isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: tantalum solid electrolytic capacitor having a low equivalent series resistance
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of polypyrrole particles. The polypyrrole layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 5 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The tantalum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 125 degrees C storage.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a tantalum anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 16 V.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% with the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin samarium-doped ceria electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The samarium-doped ceria solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 600 to 750 degrees C. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The anode support contains nickel oxide and samarium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. A 10 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 700 degrees C. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 20 seconds to a step change of sulfur dioxide concentration at 700 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum fluoride conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for sulfur dioxide. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The auxiliary electrode of sodium carbonate makes the sensor selective to sulfur dioxide against interfering gases.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects sulfur dioxide.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. Polysulfide dissolution from the titanium disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The carbon coating on the titanium disulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, carbon nanotubes, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Amperometric hydrogen sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The multilayer structure with the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. The ceramic is NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of hydrogen.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium manganite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 700 to 850 degrees C. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 500 to 650 degrees C operating range. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The thin 5 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Amperometric carbon dioxide sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The lanthanum strontium manganite electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The protective layer improves the durability of the yttria-stabilized zirconia sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of carbon dioxide concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting carbon dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

assignee_raw: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
assignee_db_group: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The capacity retention of 92% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The content of P2O5 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition for lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 8 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The scandia-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 600 to 750 degrees C. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the scandia-stabilized zirconia cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The anode support contains nickel oxide and yttria-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The thin 8 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. The reversible cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 97% or more.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor element with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer and a carbon cathode layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a niobium solid electrolytic capacitor with a low equivalent series resistance and a high rated voltage. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. The equivalent series resistance is 15 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The niobium anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) is doped with p-toluenesulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion.
