A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polycarbonate matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 600 to 750 degrees C. The reversible cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The anode support contains nickel oxide and lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite is a dense ceramic of 98% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 92% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin samarium-doped ceria electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of samarium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium difluorophosphate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The cold isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin samarium-doped ceria electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin samarium-doped ceria electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The solid electrolyte of samarium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 95% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 10 micrometers. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers and a relative density of 95%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising samarium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 10 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO LTD
title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. The cell operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The thin 8 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 700 to 850 degrees C.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 10 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The cell can be operated at 500 to 650 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 10 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 700 to 850 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 700 to 850 degrees C. The cell operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. With 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. With 1 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The 1.5 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising iron sulfide and porous carbon and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a iron sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of iron sulfide. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 100 cycles is also described. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. Polysulfide dissolution from the iron sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; iron sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 600 to 750 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The reversible cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The scandia-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 96%. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Amperometric hydrogen sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The multilayer structure with the sodium beta-alumina ceramic allows mass production by co-firing.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of hydrogen.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The Li3PS4 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: This disclosure concerns a surface mount capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode and a lead frame. The dispersion of polyaniline gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 220 microfarad rating. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor withstands 105 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the aluminum capacitor. The capacitor rated at 16 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the aluminum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The polyaniline is doped with naphthalenesulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polyaniline particles doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The roll pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: A solid electrolytic capacitor includes a porous tantalum anode body, a dielectric oxide film formed on the anode body, a conductive polymer layer comprising polyaniline doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a carbon layer, and a silver layer. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. A capacitance of 100 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The polyaniline is doped with naphthalenesulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. The tantalum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The tantalum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous tantalum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polyaniline particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Disclosed is a thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

assignee_raw: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
assignee_db_group: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
