first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor with improved heat resistance at 150 degrees C
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The polyaniline is doped with polystyrene sulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. A power module combining the capacitor with a lithium battery is also described. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 150 degrees C storage. The capacitor has a capacitance of 47 microfarads, a rated voltage of 25 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 10 milliohms at 100 kHz. The capacitor rated at 25 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polyaniline particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The silicon content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor shows a response time of 20 seconds to a step change of oxygen concentration at 500 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of barium carbonate makes the sensor selective to oxygen against interfering gases. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The oxygen sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting oxygen, comprising: a ceramic body comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate; a sensing electrode comprising platinum disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 650 to 800 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 96%. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The anode support contains nickel oxide and lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. A power density of 0.8 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The thin 8 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 0.8 W/cm2. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 500 to 650 degrees C. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: aluminum solid electrolytic capacitor having a low equivalent series resistance
abstract: This disclosure concerns a surface mount capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode and a lead frame. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the aluminum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The equivalent series resistance is 15 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The capacitor rated at 10 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 150 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous aluminum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polypyrrole particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Described is a combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 600 to 750 degrees C. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The stack shows stable operation over 50 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 600 to 750 degrees C. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers and a relative density of 98%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising samarium-doped ceria; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range. The reversible cell with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The thin 3 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. The solid electrolyte layer of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.15 or less. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell and a sensing cell on a zirconia substrate
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the sulfur dioxide concentration into an ionic activity. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The limiting current is proportional to the sulfur dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The multilayer structure with the yttria-stabilized zirconia ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The sensor detects sulfur dioxide with high selectivity and a response time of 10 seconds.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of sulfur dioxide.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The warm isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The capacity retention of 90% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 15 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The reversible cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The LATP, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The warm isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. With hafnium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The LLZO and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, vinylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding vinylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15.
