The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises nickel sulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. A lithium-sulfur battery with the nickel sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The capacity retention of 88% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A precursor of the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. A power density of 0.8 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 10 micrometers. The gadolinium-doped ceria solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising gadolinium-doped ceria; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY Co., Ltd.
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Multilayer ceramic gas sensor element and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The solid electrolyte of sodium beta-alumina conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of sulfur dioxide concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The sensor detects sulfur dioxide with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for sulfur dioxide. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium nitrite in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects sulfur dioxide.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 10% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 30 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin samarium-doped ceria electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 5 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 650 to 800 degrees C is described. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 96%. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with porous carbon by ball milling. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising molybdenum disulfide, porous carbon, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the molybdenum disulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

assignee_raw: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
assignee_db_group: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor element with a polypyrrole layer and a carbon cathode layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a surface mount capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode and a lead frame. The anode body is a sintered pellet of aluminum powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 125 degrees C storage. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The capacitor rated at 16 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polypyrrole particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 1.2 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles. A hybrid system in which the fuel cell charges a lithium ion battery is also described. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. The stack shows stable operation over 50 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Potentiometric nitrogen oxide sensor having an auxiliary electrode of barium carbonate
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. The auxiliary electrode of barium carbonate makes the sensor selective to nitrogen oxide against interfering gases. The sensor operating at 400 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for nitrogen oxide. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The ceramic is NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 400 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising barium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding vinylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The resulting LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The substitution amount is 10 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A solid electrolytic capacitor includes a porous aluminum anode body, a dielectric oxide film formed on the anode body, a conductive polymer layer comprising polyaniline doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a carbon layer, and a silver layer. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 150 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The anode body is a sintered pellet of aluminum powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The naphthalenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 150 degrees C storage. The solid electrolyte is the conductive polymer layer that serves as the true cathode of the capacitor. The equivalent series resistance is 8 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous aluminum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polyaniline particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria with a thickness of 10 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the gadolinium-doped ceria cell. The anode support contains nickel oxide and gadolinium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 600 to 750 degrees C. The gadolinium-doped ceria solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for nitrogen oxide with improved response time
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 500 degrees C. The nitrogen oxide sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 500 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The limiting current is proportional to the nitrogen oxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for nitrogen oxide. The ceramic is NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and graphene and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The confinement of nickel sulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising nickel sulfide, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the nickel sulfide is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
