A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The uniaxial pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The LiF material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers and a relative density of 97%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 650 to 800 degrees C. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Method for forming a conductive polymer layer on a dielectric oxide of a solid electrolytic capacitor
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the aluminum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the aluminum capacitor. A capacitance of 220 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The p-toluenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 150 degrees C storage.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polypyrrole particles doped with p-toluenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the indium in a lithium indium chloride framework. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a nickel sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. A separator coated with porous carbon traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising nickel sulfide, porous carbon, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the nickel sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 500 to 650 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 95% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 3 micrometers. The reversible cell with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The capacity retention of 90% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 92% of its capacity after 500 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. With tin substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The low electronic conductivity of the Li2ZrO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li3YCl6 and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the moisture stability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The roll pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The resulting Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The warm isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; iron sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The yttria-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The cell can be operated at 500 to 650 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The stack shows stable operation over 50 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers. The reversible cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the yttria-stabilized zirconia cell. The anode support contains nickel oxide and yttria-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. A 10 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 10 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The resulting Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The Li3PS4 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The Li3N layer of 50 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a titanium disulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; titanium disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

assignee_db_group: RALOSTUS ENERGY G M B H
title: Potentiometric oxygen sensor having an auxiliary electrode of sodium carbonate
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a gold electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the oxygen concentration. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of sodium carbonate makes the sensor selective to oxygen against interfering gases. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The sensing electrode comprises gold and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO LTD
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 10 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 650 to 800 degrees C is described. The reversible cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The anode support contains nickel oxide and yttria-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 650 to 800 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 650 to 800 degrees C. A 10 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more.
